To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the activation of acetyl CoA carboxylases from rat liver and Escherichia coli by citrate is a two-step process.
the activation and polymerization of acetyl-Co A carboxylase are not concerted and that the rate-limiting step of the polymerization process is a dimerization of activated protomers.
the activation of acetyl CoA carboxylas by citrate is not concerted with the polymerization of the activated protomer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanisms of activation of acyl-CoA carboxy-lase by citrate and malonyl-Co A.
the mechanism of activation of acyl-CoA carboxylation in plants.
the regulation of the enzyme acetyl-CoA-carboxylase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
citrate binds to carboxylase and induces conformational changes that activate the carboxylating activity and promote polymerization.

citrate-induced activation of acetyl CoA carboxylases is an ordered, sequential process in which the protomer of the enzyme is activated before it can polymerize, and that the activation constant of the protomer for citrate is increased by increasing concentrations of the reaction product.

the activation of acetylCoA carboxylases by citrate is a two step process, involving the formation of a citrate-activated monomer, which then polymerizes into filaments, which are the active form of the enzyme in the presence of malonyl-Coa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
citrate binds to the carboxyl-ase to activate it for catalysis.
the rate-limiting step in citrate-induced polymerization of the 450K protomer is dimerization.
the rate of activation of carboxylate protomers by citrate is rapid and is the rate-limiting step in the polymerization process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanism of activation of acyl carrier protein (ACP)-dependent acetyl-CoA (Ac-CoA) carboxylase (ACCase) is not concerted with the polymerization of protomeric ACCase.
the rate of polymer formation is rate-limiting in the citrate activation mechanism, and that the rate-limiting step is not the formation of an enzymatically active protomer.
the activation of the enzyme by citrate and the subsequent polymerization of active protomers are independent processes and that the activation of catalysis precedes polymerization.
